decisions.reason: The derivations use different labels and produce different secrets: server application traffic versus exporter master.
The derivations use different labels and produce different secrets: client application traffic versus exporter master.
The supported_versions requirement applies to different outbound messages, HelloRetryRequest and ServerHello.
The transition starts from different client states, WAIT_CERT_CR and WAIT_CERT, so the state-machine checks are separate.
Ignoring an unknown cipher suite and ignoring an unknown signature algorithm exercise different ClientHello fields.
The identical size range constrains different vectors: certificate_extension_values and OIDFilterExtension.filters.
Ignoring an unknown cipher suite and ignoring an unknown named group exercise different ClientHello fields.
ClientHello and ServerHello select different PreSharedKeyExtension body types, OfferedPsks and uint16 selected_identity.
The constraints target different message fields and have different minimum lengths: EncryptedExtensions.extensions permits zero bytes, while CertificateRequest.extensions requires at least two.
Both require different keys for multiple tickets on one connection; the canonical requirement states the atomic check and forbidden key reuse more directly.
ClientHello and ServerHello require different extension_data representations, OfferedPsks and uint16 selected_identity.
A generally prohibited extension and an otherwise defined ServerHello extension that was not offered are different invalidity conditions.
The checks constrain different enum types and different encoded maxima: HandshakeType at 255 and ExtensionType at 65535.
Both prohibit a server from sending post-handshake CertificateRequest unless the client offered post_handshake_auth; the canonical evidence is the direct primary-body MUST NOT.
The same length range applies to different fields in EncryptedExtensions and CertificateEntry.
Supporting X25519 key exchange and implementing the supported_groups extension are separate capabilities.
Both assign numeric value 1 to psk_dhe_ke; the canonical requirement uses the primary-body grammar rather than the repeated appendix definition.
The checks constrain different enum types and different encoded maxima: ContentType at 255 and ExtensionType at 65535.
Supporting X25519 key exchange and implementing the key_share extension are separate capabilities.
Implementing a particular cipher suite and implementing supported_versions are different implementation checks.
Parsing an unknown enum value at the field wire width and subsequently ignoring that parsed value are separate conjunctive checks.
The requirements authenticate different peers and differ in optionality: selected client authentication versus mandatory server authentication.
The required signature schemes differ, and rsa_pss_rsae_sha256 is scoped to certificates while ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256 is a separate supported scheme.
Supporting secp256r1 key exchange and implementing supported_versions are separate capabilities.
Consulting the recording store is one step; accepting 0-RTT after finding no match is a later step under an additional condition.
Implementing a particular cipher suite and implementing the cookie extension are different implementation checks.

Different Handshake.msg_type values select different body structures, ServerHello and Finished.

Implementing a particular cipher suite and implementing the server_name extension are different implementation checks.
Implementing TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and implementing signature_algorithms_cert are different implementation checks.
The triggering hash algorithms and normative strengths differ: MD5 requires abort, whereas SHA-1 abort is recommended.
Choosing a collision-resistant underlying hash and enforcing a minimum HKDF-Expand output length are separate conjuncts.
The receiver direction and containing messages differ: a server parsing ClientHello versus a client parsing NewSessionTicket.
Opposite client-authentication branches from WAIT_FLIGHT2 enter different target states, WAIT_CERT and WAIT_FINISHED.

Implementing a particular cipher suite and implementing supported_groups are different implementation checks.
Different Handshake.msg_type values select different body structures, Certificate and KeyUpdate.
Supporting rsa_pkcs1_sha256 certificate signatures and supporting X25519 key exchange are unrelated capabilities.
Both require a server to ignore an unrecognized ClientHello extension; the canonical requirement is the direct primary-body MUST.
Implementing TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 and implementing signature_algorithms_cert are different implementation checks.
The supported_versions presence check applies to different messages, ServerHello and HelloRetryRequest.
The same allowed message set applies to different extension types, server_name and use_srtp.
The extension types and allowed message sets differ: cookie is CH/HRR, while supported_versions is CH/SH/HRR.
Supporting secp256r1 key exchange and implementing supported_groups are separate capabilities.
The checks constrain different enum types and maxima: ExtensionType at 65535 and CertificateType at 255.

Supporting secp256r1 key exchange and implementing key_share are separate capabilities.

Supporting X25519 key exchange and implementing the cookie extension are separate capabilities.

Using the corresponding hash for the mask-generation digest and for the signed digest are separate conjunctive checks.
Proceeding with the handshake and avoiding actions that assume freshness are separate required behaviors from the same out-of-tolerance condition.
